bull_case_summary: Oracle has realised IaaS revenue growth and improved revenue/EPS. Round two distinguishes existing conversion from the enormous future contract book and preserves conditional growth with financing discipline rather than treating RPO as cash.
bear_case_summary: The bear accepts existing conversion but retains debt, leases, FCF and future-capacity funding as unresolved. Higher policy rates raise a general hurdle without proving company repricing, and low forward estimates do not price obligations.
key_points_of_agreement: Some cloud activity already converts into revenue.
The $664bn RPO is future contracted activity rather than cash received.
Prior revenue conversion does not automatically finance the next expansion.
Mixed technical recovery supplies little additional support.
key_points_of_disagreement: How much demonstrated conversion capability strengthens prospective returns before next-stage capacity funding is reconciled.
unresolved_uncertainties: Debt, leases, FCF and matched operating-to-cash bridge.
Funding and investment returns on capacity required for backlog delivery.
Normalised valuation independent of vendor forward estimates.
